title: Call-surface sanitizer and concordance runtime
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Customers and partner integrations send a wide variety of tool/function call shapes: legacy 'function' objects, OpenAI-style 'tool' schemas, informal names, and sometimes corrupted/partial JSON in streaming outputs. This causes incorrect routing, silent failures, and manual fixes in adapters. Goal: build a lightweight runtime component that sanitizes call signatures, normalizes naming to a canonical registry, and enforces structured-output guarantees (complete JSON objects for tool payloads) while preserving streaming semantics and low tail latency.

Scope: the component ("concordance runtime") sits in the inference request path prior to the router. It provides:
- Name concordance: fuzzy/phonetic matching (double-metaphone + token-weighted edit distance) to map incoming tool/function names to canonical identifiers.
- Signature sanitizer: normalize param shapes, coerce numeric/string types where safe, and explicitly reject ambiguous/ambiguous-optional fields with a clear error for SDKs.
- Streaming-aware assembly: reassemble chunked/partial JSON emitted during streaming responses into validated structured payloads; emit partial tool-call events for observability but only route when a complete structured payload is recovered or a deterministic fallback applies.
- Backcompat shim: translate legacy function formats to the modern tool contract (and vice versa when returning responses) with an extensible ruleset driven by a registry stored in Redis for low-latency lookups.
- Failover policy: deterministic fallback behaviors (soft-fail to best-match with telemetry flag, hard-fail with explicit error, or queue for human review depending on customer tier).

Design notes:
- Implementation will be a small Rust service compiled into the serving path (same host as the router) to avoid cross-host RPC. We prefer zero-copy parsing where possible and will use serde with a streaming JSON parser to reconstruct partial payloads.
- Name registry: canonical_name -> aliases (regex + phonetic keys + historical aliases). Aliases include versions and known typo patterns. The registry is append-only by default; mutations go through a supported API and are audited.
- Telemetry: record match confidence, sanitization actions (coerced fields, dropped attributes), and time-to-completion for streaming assemble. Surface aggregated rollback triggers in the Console rollout dashboard.
- Migration: start with a read-only concordance mode (observe matches, no automatic rewrites) for two weeks, then enable auto-translation for low-risk mappings at 5% traffic, 25%, 100% after monitoring.

Success criteria:
- Reduce misrouted tool calls by 95% for customers in the canary pool.
- No more than 2% p90 latency regression on the critical request path for low-latency plans.
- Structured-output validation errors reduced by 80% in first 30 days after GA.

Open questions:
- What should the definitive policy be for numeric-vs-string coercion across customer datasets? (security and semantics concerns)
- How aggressive should automatic alias creation be when confidence is borderline?

Artifacts and links:
- API spec draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Call+Surface+Concordance+Spec
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1428
- Observability dashboard (canary): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/call-concordance-canary

Rollout plan: canary -> dedicated customers -> hosted-wide with feature flag, include a manual rollback switch in Console and automated rollback when error rates exceed thresholds.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ava Chen: Ticket created after customer postmortem (INC-2026-013). Root cause: non-deterministic tool name variants + streaming partial JSON. Assigned to Miguel for implementation spike.

2026-02-12 - Miguel Torres: Spike completed. Double-metaphone + token-weighted edit distance gives good recall on our internal corpus (recall 0.92, precision 0.89). Prototype parser reassembled 98% of partial tool payloads in synthetic streaming tests. Link to prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1428

2026-02-14 - Samir Patel (arch review): Asked for explicit tracing IDs on reconstructed payloads so we can link streaming segments back to original token offsets. Also requested audit trail for any automatic alias creation. Marked security_review_required = true.

2026-02-16 - Lina Morales (Design): UX note — when we auto-rewrite names, surface the mapping in the Console logs with a reversible token so customers can opt out per-namespace. Also recommended adding a per-route toggle for aggressive vs conservative mapping.

2026-02-18 - Miguel Torres: Implemented the registry as Redis-backed with local LRU cache (ttl 5m) to keep lookups O(1) and reduce cross-host latency. Added metric: concordance_match_confidence (0-1). Draft PR opened for integration tests.

2026-02-19 - QA: Found an edge case where streaming segments containing escape sequences caused the assembler to drop fields. Repro steps and fixture attached to PR. Miguel investigating a safer parser fallback.

2026-02-20 - Miguel Torres: Fixed parser fallback, added fuzzing for edge-case streams, and pushed new integration tests. Planning canary deployment for 2026-02-24. Blocker: needs security review signoff for registry mutation API (see ENG-88122 as security ticket).
